data.narrative:
Itera is a seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised $12M to date, led by CEO AJ Cooper (PhD EE, ex-Uber Jump/Lyft hardware) alongside founders with backgrounds at Verkada, Bridgewater, and VMware. The Chips & Semiconductors sector comprises 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched, though no narrow peer set of sufficient size exists at identical stage and valuation tier.

Given data constraints, only the Stage-Progression method is applicable. Using $12M total raised as a proxy for valuation and applying a typical 2.5x Seed-to-next-stage multiplier yields an implied valuation of $30M. The Peer-Median approach is not viable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables in the narrow peer set (0 same-stage, 2 adjacent-stage identified). Public-Comp Anchoring cannot be applied because Itera's revenue is not disclosed; while public semiconductors trade at a median 20.4x P/S, this multiple requires material revenue visibility unavailable for private companies at seed stage.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M–$34M, centered on $30M. Key uncertainties include the lack of revenue data, absence of near-peer seed/Series A comparables with disclosed terms, and stage-progression assumptions that may not reflect Itera's specific market position or burn rate. Validation would require either market-rate Series A pricing or disclosure of material revenue or technical milestones.
